extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Health Insurance Exchanges (Marketplaces), health insurance issuers, State governments, and stakeholders submitting comments to CMS/HHS on the proposed 2026 Payment Notice and related Exchange rules
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed CMS/HHS rulemaking on (1) requiring and standardizing pre-enrollment eligibility verification for Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) across Exchanges and (2) amending EHB rules to prohibit coverage of 'sex‑trait modification' as an Essential Health Benefit beginning PY 2026, plus changes to the premium adjustment percentage methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require all Exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment SEP eligibility verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.420(g) to require all Exchanges (including Exchanges on the Federal platform and State Exchanges) to conduct pre-enrollment eligibility verification for Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This removes the current limitation that Federal platform Exchanges only conduct pre-enrollment verification for the loss of minimum essential coverage SEP and would reinstate pre-enrollment verification for other SEPs; intended to reduce misuse and abuse of SEPs and improve program integrity and the risk pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: 75 percent verification threshold for new SEP enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require that Exchanges conduct SEP verification for at least 75 percent of new enrollments through SEPs for consumers not already enrolled in coverage through the applicable Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 75 percent threshold was chosen based on current SEP verification volumes and is intended to be achievable by verifying the two or three largest SEP types. Determination of how many enrollments constitute 75 percent must be based on enrollment through all SEPs, allowing Exchanges flexibility to choose which SEP types to verify. CMS seeks comment on whether the threshold should be based on past year enrollments, projections, or another metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of unsuccessful verification on enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Exchange is unable to verify the consumer's eligibility for enrollment through the SEP, then the consumer is not eligible for enrollment through the Exchange under that SEP, and any plan selection under that SEP must be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an enrollment under an SEP for which eligibility cannot be verified becomes effectuated, the enrollment may be terminated in accordance with §155.430(b)(2)(i). If an Exchange pends a plan selection prior to enrollment and cannot verify eligibility, the consumer would be found ineligible and the plan selection would not result in enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchanges not required to verify all SEP types (cost‑benefit flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges would not be required to verify eligibility for every SEP; they may choose which SEP types to verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS recognizes that verifying SEP-triggering events with very low volumes could cost more than the benefit of verification; Exchanges may focus verification on higher-volume SEP types to meet the 75 percent threshold while avoiding undue cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchanges may propose alternative verification methods under §155.315(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: State Exchanges have flexibility under §155.315(h) to propose alternative methods for conducting required verifications that reduce administrative costs and burdens while maintaining accuracy and minimizing delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to use §155.315(h) authority to allow State Exchanges to request HHS approval for alternative SEP verification processes as part of determining eligibility under §155.305(b). This permits coordination between State Exchanges and HHS to design approaches appropriate for specific populations and technical capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timeline for SEP verification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to allow Exchanges until the 2026 benefit year (PY 2026) to implement SEP verification requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS recognizes State Exchanges may need additional time and seeks comment and suggestions to alleviate implementation burdens and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evidentiary standard for pre-enrollment verification impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use empirical enrollment and verification metrics to assess the impact of pre-enrollment verification on SEP use, continuous enrollment, and the risk pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites metrics such as response time to document review (1–3 days in PY 2017), percent of applicants able to submit documents within 14 or 30 days, percent unable to resolve SVIs, changes in enrollment duration, changes in partial-year enrollment factors, loss ratios for SEP vs OEP enrollments, and issuer-level disenrollment percentages to justify policy decisions and to monitor future impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit comments on measurement base for verification threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether the 75 percent verification threshold should be based on past-year SEP enrollments, future-year projections, or another appropriate metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS acknowledges unforeseen events may change SEP volume year-to-year and invites States to comment on feasibility of applying pre-enrollment verification beyond the 75 percent baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit sex‑trait modification as an Essential Health Benefit (EHB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §156.115(d) to provide that issuers of non-grandfathered individual and small group market coverage may not provide coverage for 'sex‑trait modification' as an EHB beginning with PY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states the legal basis that EHB must be equal in scope to a typical employer plan and asserts sex‑trait modification is not typically included in employer plans. The proposal does not prevent plans from voluntarily covering sex‑trait modification as a non‑EHB (subject to State law) nor prevent States from mandating coverage (which would trigger defrayal obligations). CMS also requests comment on the proposed change and its impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for definition and scope of 'sex‑trait modification'
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is not proposing a formal definition of 'sex‑trait modification' but solicits comment on whether a definition should be adopted and how to account for items/services currently covered or excluded by plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS also requests information on current issuer standards for what is considered 'sex‑trait modification' and how a definition could best capture items and services that plans treat as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of medical-condition exceptions to the EHB prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS recognizes some items/services used for sex‑trait modification may be appropriate for other medical conditions (e.g., precocious puberty, therapy after traumatic injury) and seeks comment on whether explicit exceptions should be defined to permit coverage of such items/services as EHB for those other conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS asks commenters to specify what conditions should be excepted for potential inclusion in a final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: State mandate and defrayal consequences for sex‑trait modification coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State mandates coverage of sex‑trait modification outside its EHB‑benchmark plan, the State would be required to defray the cost of that mandated benefit per §155.170.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sex‑trait modification is removed from a State's EHB‑benchmark plan at a future date, the State may have to defray costs under §155.170 when the benefit is no longer an EHB. CMS will enforce defrayal obligations consistent with statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date solicitation for EHB prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose PY 2026 as the effective date for prohibiting sex‑trait modification as an EHB and seek comment on the impact of that timing or whether an earlier or later effective date is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS specifically solicits comments on how the proposed timing would affect coverage in individual, small group, and large group markets for PY 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update premium adjustment percentage methodology to include individual market premiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to update §156.130(e) methodology to establish a premium growth measure that captures premium changes in the individual market in addition to employer‑sponsored insurance (ESI) premiums for PY 2026 and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes calculating the premium adjustment percentage for PY 2026 and beyond using an adjusted private individual and group market health insurance premium measure similar to the NHEA private health insurance premium measure. The rule would set values for the PY 2026 premium adjustment percentage, maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, reduced maximum annual limitations on cost sharing, and required contribution percentage, superseding earlier guidance (October 2024 PAPI Guidance) if finalized as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of an adjusted private individual and group market premium measure (NHEA‑like)
rubrics_metrics.description: The premium adjustment percentage calculation would use an adjusted private private individual and group market premium measure similar to NHEA's private health insurance premium measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHEA's private health insurance premium measure includes premiums for ESI, 'direct purchase insurance' (individual market purchased directly from issuers, on and off Exchanges), Medigap insurance, and the medical portion of accident ('property and casualty') insurance. CMS frames this reversion to a broader measure as responsive to stabilization of premium trends post‑PHE.
